[[File:Bockaert.jpg|thumb|Joël Bockaert, Member of the French Academy of science]]
'''Joël Bockaert''' (born 3 October 1945, in [[Roubaix]]) is a French [[biologist]].

== Biography ==
He was a student at the École Normale d'Instituteur in [[Mérignac, Gironde|Mérignac]] (33) from 1961 to 1964 and at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale supérieure]]-Rue d'Ulm-Paris from 1964 to 1968.

Graduate in [[Natural science|Natural Sciences]] (1968), he completed his thesis work at the [[Collège de France]] and his post-doctoral internship at [[Northwestern University]] in [[Chicago]]. He was successively a professor at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|University of Paris VI]] (1968–73), deputy director of the Chair of [[Cell physiology|Cell Physiology]] at the Collège de France (1973–82) before being, in [[Montpellier]], Director of Research at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]] (1982-2001) then Professor at the [[University of Montpellier]] (2001-2014).

In Montpellier, he founded the CNRS-INSERM Institute of [[Pharmacology]]-[[Endocrinology]] (1982), of which he was Director from 1990 to 2005 and then the Institute of [[Functional genomics|Functional Genomics]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Institut de génomique fonctionnelle|url=https://www.igf.cnrs.fr/index.php/fr/|publication-date=}}</ref> In 2013, he became Director of the Biology and Health Department of Montpellier.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|title=Pôle Biologie-Santé de Montpellier|url=https://www.polebiosante-rabelais.fr/|publication-date=|access-date=2019-11-12|archive-date=2019-02-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190219015724/https://www.polebiosante-rabelais.fr/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Scientific work ==
Joël Bockaert's work has been devoted to the study of intercellular communications and in particular those involved in the [[brain]].<ref>Bockaert J, « Molecular tinkering of G protein-coupled receptors: an evolutionary success », ''Embo Journal'', (1999) 18, <abbr>p.</abbr> 1723-1729</ref><ref>Joël Bockaert, La communication du vivant, Paris, Odile Jacob, 2017</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Canal Académie|url=https://www.canalacademie.com/idm1276-+-Joel-BOCKAERT-+.html|publication-date=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Maison de la chimie|date=9 April 2018 |url=https://vimeopro.com/maisondelachimie/chimie-et-cerveau/video/263844817}}</ref>

Joël Bockaert was one of the pioneers in the study of molecules responsible for recognizing and interpreting the messages of intercellular communication known as "receptors". He specialized in the study of a family of receptors called "[[G protein|G-protein]] coupled receptors or GPCGs". He will discover some of them, including [[oxytocin]], [[vasopressin]],<ref>Jard S, « Stimulus-response coupling in neurohypophysial peptide target cells. », ''Physiological  Review'', 1975 (5554), <abbr>p.</abbr> 489-536</ref> metabotropic brain [[Glutamic acid|glutamate]]<ref>Sladeczek F., « Glutamate stiumates inositol phosphate formation in striatal neurones », ''Nature'', (1985) 317, <abbr>p.</abbr> 717-719</ref><ref>Dumuis A, « Arachidonic acid released from striatal neurons by joint stimulation of ionotropic and metabotropic quisqualate receptors », ''Nature'', (1990) 347, <abbr>p.</abbr> 182-4</ref><ref>Ango, F, « Agonist independent activation of mGluRs by intracellular protein Homer », ''Nature'', (2001) 411, <abbr>p.</abbr> 962-966</ref><ref>Dumuis A., « NMDA receptors activate the arachidonic acid cascade system in striatal neurons. », ''Nature'', (1988) 336, <abbr>p.</abbr> 68-70</ref><ref>Lafon-Cazal M., « NMDA-dependent superoxide production and neurotoxicity », ''Nature'', (1993)   364, <abbr>p.</abbr> 535-537</ref><ref>Bertaso F, « PICK1 uncoupling from mGluR7a causes absence-like seizures », ''Nature Neuroscience'', (2008) 8, <abbr>p.</abbr> 940-8</ref> and [[serotonin]]<ref>Bockaert J, « 5-HT(4) receptors, a place in the sun: act two », ''Curr Opin Pharmacol.'', (2011) 11, <abbr>p.</abbr> 87-93</ref> receptors.  The latter modulate cognitive and emotional functions. The family of GPCRs is of considerable physiological importance. It is these receptors that capture light (ensuring vision), which recognize bitter, sweet or umami tastes, smells but also the majority of hormones and neurotransmitters1,2.

Given their roles, these receptors are the direct or indirect target of more than 40% of drugs sold in pharmacies to treat hypertension, allergies, migraine, depression, parkinson's disease or pain.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

== Societies and academies ==
   1992-1995 President of the Society of Neurosciences

   1996: Member of EMBO

He was elected a corresponding member of the French Academy of sciences in 1996 and a member in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|title=Académie des sciences|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-B/joel-bockaert.html|publication-date=}}</ref>

In 2017, he became a member of the Academy of sciences and letters of Montpellier

== Awards and honours ==

*    Rochat-Julliard Prize of the French Academy of sciences
*    Charles-Léopold Mayer Grand Prize of the Academy of Sciences  
*    Lilly - [[European College of Neuropsychopharmacology|ECNP]] Prize
*    Honorary Professor of [[Huachung University|Huazhong University]] (China) and recipient of the China and Friendship Award
*    Doctor Honoris Causa [[Université libre de Bruxelles]]

=== Decorations ===

*    Chevalier of the [[Legion of Honour|Légion d'Honneur]]
*    Chevalier of the [[Ordre des Palmes académiques|Palmes Académiques]]
